input.question: If Voyager 1 is travelling at a speed of 38,000mph, and if just a small piece of space debris collides with it, wouldn't the probe break or have a major alteration in its course because of the immense speed?
input.ground_truth: The interstellar medium has a very low density, ~10^-4 ions/cm^3, this (roughly) equates to 1cm^3 of matter per cube of space, with a side length of 10,000 km. And most of that material will be individual ions. The chance of hitting anything out there is very remote.

Okay, let’s imagine Voyager 1 is like a super fast toy car, and it’s zooming really, really fast—faster than any car you’ve ever seen! Now, imagine there’s a tiny pebble in space. If that pebble hits Voyager 1, even though Voyager is moving super fast, the pebble is still just a tiny pebble.

Because the pebble is so small, when it hits Voyager, it’s not like a big truck hitting the car. It’s more like a tiny raindrop hitting your window. The Voyager is strong and made to handle space, but even so, if something hits it really hard and really fast, it could get hurt or change direction a little bit. But because space is almost empty, there aren’t many pebbles to hit it.

So, if a tiny piece of space “pebble” hits Voyager 1, it might get a little bump or scratch, but because Voyager is tough and the pebble is so small, it probably won’t break unless it’s a really big piece. And if it does hit, Voyager might wiggle a tiny bit, but not go flying off in a totally different direction unless it’s a big hit.
